errors: The claim that the α-class is always exactly half of the residues prime to 4n fails in degenerate cases. For p^2 - nq^2 with n a perfect square, every odd number prime to n is a divisor. Euler tacitly excludes this.

Moment (6) is not a proof and is in a sense circular. Multiplicative closure and the index-2 structure cannot by themselves decide which primes lie in the divisor set; that is exactly the content of quadratic reciprocity. Euler frames it honestly as probability.

The step 'from some found values all others follow by products' is true only if the found values generate the subgroup. Squares alone generate only the subgroup of squares, which in general has index greater than 2.

Classes with character 2 for 37 rely on Cor. 2's merger of class 3 (3D=F) into class 2 (2D=F). This is asserted from the examples rather than proved, though it is correct here: the wide class group has order 2.

ideas.what: Assignment of characters (1 or 2) to the admissible residues mod 120 for p^2-30q^2, with the observation that each character occurs equally often
ideas.modern_name: Genus/class splitting of the kernel of the quadratic character; equal distribution of residue classes among genera

ideas.where_published: E598 itself (Opuscula analytica II, 1785); similar tables in E256/E164-type papers (unsure of exact locations)

ideas.what: Divisor residues mod 4n form a multiplicatively closed system containing squares, exactly half of the reduced residues; the complement times the complement lands in the divisor class
ideas.modern_name: Kernel of the Kronecker character as an index-2 subgroup of (Z/4nZ)*; quotient group of order 2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (implicitly), made explicit by Gauss/Dirichlet; group language later (Dedekind, Weber)
ideas.where_published: E552 'Observationes circa divisionem quadratorum per numeros primos' (Opuscula analytica I, 1783); E164; E256

ideas.what: Conjecture that all primes ≡ α mod 4n divide some p^2 ± nq^2
ideas.where_published: E164, E552, E598; discussed by Weil 'Number Theory', Lemmermeyer 'Reciprocity Laws'

ideas.what: Heuristic sieve: remove α-class composites having an 𝔄-factor; the rest, including all primes, should be divisors
ideas.modern_name: Heuristic toward reciprocity via multiplicativity of the Jacobi/Kronecker symbol
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (heuristic); Jacobi symbol multiplicativity formalized by Jacobi (1837)

deep.surprise_reason: This is Euler's well-documented reciprocity conjecture with its implicit index-2 subgroup structure, already discussed by Weil and Lemmermeyer. The 'equal number of characters' remark is a mild genus-theory anticipation, but it is known and appears in Euler's other number-theory papers.
